Marketing Manager Resume Example & Writing Guide (2026)

A marketing manager resume is judged on one question: did your marketing make money? Hiring managers — and the applicant tracking systems that screen before them — scan your resume for the signals that answer it: the pipeline you built, the conversion rates you moved, the budgets you managed, the channels you owned, and the team you led to do it.

This guide gives you a full annotated example, a section-by-section breakdown, the demand-generation keywords postings screen for, and the mistakes that quietly cost marketing managers interviews.

Quick answer: A marketing manager resume should include a summary naming your market and strongest proof (e.g. marketing manager who grew qualified pipeline 62% in one year), a skills section with demand generation, content, SEO, and marketing automation tools, experience bullets with pipeline, conversion, and revenue numbers, and keywords mirrored from the posting. Results, not activities, win interviews.

Key Takeaways

  • Lead with your market and your headline result — “marketing manager who grew qualified pipeline 62% in one year” answers the credibility question in one line.
  • Every experience bullet needs a number: pipeline generated, cost per lead, conversion rate, revenue influenced, budget managed. “Ran campaigns” is an activity; “cut cost per lead 28% while growing pipeline to $2.4M” is evidence.
  • Spell tools exactly as postings do — HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Analytics, Google Ads — they are literal ATS keyword filters.
  • Name the team and budget scope you owned. “Led a team of 6 and a $480K annual budget” tells a hiring manager what level you can step into.
  • Keep the layout single-column with standard headings. Fancy graphics don’t parse. Verify with a free ATS scan before you apply.

What Marketing Hiring Managers Actually Look For

Ask the VP of marketing or founder doing the hiring what separates a keep-forever marketing manager from a risky one and it won’t be “creative.” It’ll be:

  • Pipeline proof. Qualified pipeline generated, demos booked, trials started, revenue influenced — with numbers attached. “Grew qualified pipeline 62% to $2.4M in 12 months” is the line everything else supports.
  • Channel ownership. Content, SEO, paid media, email, events, partnerships — name the channels you actually owned, not every channel you touched once. Depth in two or three channels beats a shallow list of ten.
  • Efficiency, not just spend. Cost per lead down, conversion rate up, payback period shortened. Managers who can show they made each dollar work harder get the bigger budgets.
  • Cross-functional credibility. Sales alignment, product launches with product teams, agency management, executive reporting.
  • Team leadership. People hired, coached, and retained; freelancers and agencies managed; a content calendar or campaign cadence you ran. Even one direct report, managed well, counts.

Marketing Manager Resume Example (Annotated)

Below is a complete example for a marketing manager in a B2B software company. It’s fictional — the names and companies are illustrative — but every bullet follows the pattern marketing hiring managers respond to: the market up front, numbers on every role, and the demand-generation vocabulary spelled exactly as postings use it.

ELENA MARSH
Abuja, FCT · (234) 555-0147 · elena.marsh@email.com · elenamarsh.example/portfolio

SUMMARY
Marketing manager with 6 years growing B2B software brands. Grew qualified pipeline 62% to $2.4M in 12 months; cut cost per lead 28% while lifting demo conversion 41%. Led a team of 6 and managed a $480K annual budget across content, paid media, and events.

SKILLS
Demand generation · Content marketing · SEO · Paid media (Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads) · Email and lifecycle marketing · Marketing automation (HubSpot, Marketo) · Analytics (Google Analytics, attribution) · Team leadership · Brand campaigns · Product launches · Salesforce · A/B testing

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Marketing Manager — Northbeam Software, Abuja | 2022–Present

  • Own demand generation for a B2B SaaS product: grew qualified pipeline 62% to $2.4M in 12 months across content, paid, and partnerships.
  • Cut cost per lead 28% by rebuilding paid audiences and landing pages; lifted demo conversion 41% with a new trial-nurture email sequence.
  • Lead a team of 6 (content, paid, design) and manage a $480K annual budget; run a weekly campaign cadence with sales alignment reviews.
  • Launched 3 product releases with product and sales: launch pages, webinars, and partner announcements drove 1,800+ registrations per launch.
  • Built the content engine from 4 to 18 posts a month; organic search now drives 34% of qualified pipeline, up from 12%.

Digital Marketing Specialist — Brightpath Agency, Abuja | 2019–2022

  • Managed paid campaigns for 8 clients across SaaS, retail, and professional services; average account spend $15K a month.
  • Ran A/B tests on ads and landing pages for 12 accounts; winning variants lifted conversion 19% on average.
  • Produced monthly performance reports for clients: spend, leads, cost per lead, and next-month recommendations in plain language.
  • Coordinated 20+ webinars and virtual events a year: registration pages, email invitations, and post-event follow-up sequences.

EDUCATION
BSc, Marketing — 2019

Section-by-Section Breakdown

Summary: market, tenure, and headline proof in three lines

The example opens with “marketing manager” — role and tenure — then the proof: pipeline up 62% to $2.4M, cost per lead down 28%, demo conversion up 41%. If you’re stepping up without a manager title, lead with owned outcomes instead: “owned the content calendar and a $15K monthly paid budget; grew organic leads 40% in a year.”

Skills: channels and tools exactly as postings spell them

Marketing postings are keyword-dense, and applicant tracking systems screen for exact terms. Name your channels (demand generation, content marketing, SEO, paid media, lifecycle marketing), your tools (HubSpot, Marketo, Salesforce, Google Analytics, Google Ads), and your leadership scope (team size, budget). “Good communicator” is not a keyword; “HubSpot” is.

Experience: every bullet pairs an action with a number

The pattern is verb + scope + metric: “grew qualified pipeline 62% to $2.4M”; “cut cost per lead 28% while lifting demo conversion 41%.” Efficiency metrics are gold — they prove you can grow results without simply spending more.

Portfolio: one defensible case study, linked cleanly

Marketing managers are judged on work people can see. Link one campaign page with its goal, channels, spend, and result — and make sure it loads fast on a phone.

Marketing Manager Skills & ATS Keywords

Mirror the posting’s exact language and keep these groups on your resume:

  • Growth: demand generation, lead generation, pipeline, conversion rate optimization, A/B testing, growth marketing.
  • Channels: content marketing, SEO, paid media, Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads, email marketing, lifecycle marketing, events.
  • Tools: HubSpot, Marketo, Salesforce, Google Analytics, attribution, marketing automation, CRM.
  • Leadership: team leadership, budget management, agency management, sales alignment, product launches, brand campaigns.

Check your resume against a free ATS scan — for example, Cvyon's ATS grader — before you apply. Marketing managers lose interviews to parsing failures they never see: two-column layouts and icon-heavy designs are the usual killers. Start from a clean template in the template gallery or the resume builder, then verify with the free ATS grader.

5 Mistakes That Cost Marketing Manager Interviews

  1. Listing activities instead of outcomes. “Ran social media campaigns” is a job description, not a resume bullet. Replace every activity with a number: pipeline generated, cost per lead, conversion lifted, revenue influenced.
  2. Claiming every channel. A list of twelve channels reads as depth in none. Name the two or three you owned, with results, and let the rest appear only where you genuinely delivered.
  3. Vague budget claims. “Managed large budgets” wastes a line. Name the number: “$480K annual budget across content, paid media, and events.” Budget scope is how hiring managers judge the step-up.
  4. No portfolio link — or a broken one. Marketing is visible work. One working case-study link beats a paragraph of adjectives, and a dead link actively hurts you. Test it on your phone before you apply.
  5. Ignoring the company’s own vocabulary. If the posting says “demand generation in HubSpot” and you write “did marketing automation,” the ATS filter never fires. Mirror the posting’s exact terms.

Frequently Asked Questions

What should be included in a marketing manager resume?

A summary naming your market and strongest proof (e.g. “marketing manager who grew qualified pipeline 62% in one year”); a skills section with demand generation, content marketing, SEO, paid media, and marketing automation tools (HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Analytics); experience bullets with pipeline, conversion, and revenue numbers; and keywords mirrored from the posting.

How do I show marketing ROI on a resume?

Pair every campaign with a before-and-after number: pipeline generated, cost per lead, conversion rate, revenue influenced, or payback period. “Ran paid social campaigns” is an activity; “cut cost per lead 28% while growing qualified pipeline 62% to $2.4M” is a return. If you cannot tie a campaign to revenue, tie it to the next closest outcome — demos booked, trials started, or qualified leads delivered.

Should a marketing manager resume include a portfolio?

Yes — link one campaign, landing page, or content piece you can defend with numbers, not a gallery of everything you ever made. One strong case study (goal, channels, spend, result) beats ten screenshots. Put the link in your summary or skills section, and make sure the page loads fast and reads well on a phone.

How long should a marketing manager resume be?

One page for most marketing manager roles, two pages only if you have 10+ years with team-lead scope and multiple channels to evidence. Hiring managers and applicant tracking systems both prefer a clean single page with standard headings. If a campaign story needs more room, put it in the portfolio, not on page two.

What skills do employers want most on a marketing manager resume?

Demand generation, content marketing, SEO, paid media (Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Meta Ads), email and lifecycle marketing, marketing automation (HubSpot, Marketo), analytics (Google Analytics, attribution), and team leadership. Channel keywords matter: HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Analytics, and the exact channels named in the posting — spell them exactly as postings do.

How do I write a marketing manager resume with no management experience?

Lead with owned outcomes, not headcount: campaigns you ran end-to-end, budgets you managed, channels you owned, and results you delivered. “Owned the content calendar for a 3-person team” and “managed a $15K monthly paid budget” both prove management-ready scope. Add cross-functional wins — sales alignment, product launches, agency management — and run it through a free ATS grader before applying.
